Thus the matrix \(M\) takes only two distinct scalar values: \(a\) on all red pixels and \(b\) on all white pixels. Without loss of generality assume \(a\neq b\). Then
\[
M=(a-b)R+bJ,
\]
where \(J\) is the all-ones matrix (rank 1) and \(R\) is the 0-1 indicator of the red set. Equivalently,
\[
\operatorname{rank}(M)=\operatorname{rank}(R+cJ)
\]

\operatorname{rank}(M)\le\operatorname{rank}(R)+1.
\]

The red set is exactly the complement (inside the bounding rectangle of the flag) of four smaller rectangles—the four white blocks created by the arms of the cross. Each rectangle indicator is an outer product of two indicator vectors and therefore has rank 1. Hence \(R\) itself is a linear combination of five rank-1 matrices and satisfies
\[
\operatorname{rank}(R)\le5.
\]
A tighter bound follows from examining the distinct row-support vectors that appear. The flag geometry partitions the rows into four contiguous horizontal bands (above the canton, the upper half of the canton, the horizontal bar of the cross, the lower half of the canton, and the remainder of the field) whose color patterns are linearly independent for generic widths. Consequently the column space of \(R+cJ\) has dimension exactly 3, which is therefore the maximal attainable rank of \(M\).

The flag of Tonga consists of a red field bearing a white canton that itself contains a red cross (Greek cross).  When the flag is rasterized on a sufficiently fine grid the resulting 0-1 matrix R (1 on every red pixel, 0 on every white pixel) therefore exhibits only three distinct row vectors:

- constant-1 rows that lie entirely outside the canton,
- rows that intersect only the vertical arm of the cross (narrow central block of 1’s),
- rows that intersect the full horizontal arm of the cross (wide central block of 1’s).

Any two of these vectors are linearly independent; their pairwise differences have disjoint supports inside the canton columns, so the three vectors themselves form a linearly independent set.  Consequently rank(R) = 3.  

The affine matrix M = (a-b)R + b J differs from a scalar multiple of R by a rank-1 all-ones matrix J.  Because the three distinct rows of R already contain a constant row, the rank-1 update is absorbed and does not increase the dimension of the row space; hence rank(M) = 3 as well.  No fourth linearly independent row pattern appears, regardless of the relative widths of the arms, so the bound is tight for every a ≠ b and every resolving grid.
